title: SESAME SALT GARNISH
release_blockers: Approved holding and storage conditions, container labeling, use-by basis and discard rule.
Second-cook reproduction with chef-approved tolerances for yield, crushing endpoint and portioning.

intro: A loose, lightly crushed sesame finish for grilled vegetables. White sesame brings the body; whole black seeds add contrast. Stop crushing while the mixture still falls freely from a spoon.
equipment: 300 mL mortar and pestle, spoon, dry scraper, dry receiving container; scale readable to 0.1 g. One 130 g input batch only.
allergens: Sesame. Simulated label review lists no additional declared allergens. Shared utensils need house cross-contact controls; no free-from claim.

stages.name: CRUSH
stages.tip: Roughly half the seeds should split. The mixture must stay loose, with no oily paste.

steps.text: Weigh white sesame (I1) into the 300 mL mortar. Use 10 press-and-turn strokes, approximately 30 seconds from the first stroke.
Check the texture: roughly half the seeds should split. The mixture must remain loose, with no oily paste.
Add black sesame (I2) and salt (I3). Stir with a spoon for 20 turns, approximately 20 seconds from the first turn. Total mortar load: 130 g.
Check that black seeds are distributed through the mixture and no salt pockets remain. Log any failed endpoint for trial review.

stages.name: WEIGH & PORTION
stages.tip: Three minutes total active preparation. Do not force actual yield to match the reference result.

steps.text: Scrape into a tared, dry container. Record actual usable mass and transfer loss. Reference trial: 128 g usable from 130 g input.
For the simulated plating trial, weigh 2.0 g per plate and sprinkle evenly across the vegetable surface immediately before dispatch. No bowl garnish.

notes.heading: Scaling & variations
notes.text: At factor 2: 200 g white sesame, 40 g black sesame and 20 g salt. Run two separate reference-size batches; weigh each output. Do not double mortar load or crushing time. Finished yield is not guaranteed. No substitutions are approved.

notes.heading: Controls & corrective action
notes.text: Check seed breakage, absence of paste, mixing and output on every trial. Record deviations for chef review. Recheck current supplier labels and house utensil controls. No validated food-safety critical control point is asserted; applicable controls await house SOP review.

notes.heading: Volume research and sources
notes.text: Volumes are researched approximations, not measurements; gram weights stay authoritative. Source 1: King Arthur Baking, Ingredient Weight Chart, https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/learn/ingredient-weight-chart, accessed 2026-10-26, listing sesame seeds at 1/2 US cup = 71 g, that is 8.875 g per US tablespoon, with US measures (1 US cup = 236.6 mL, 1 US tbsp = 14.79 mL, 1 US tsp = 4.93 mL). Source 2: USDA FoodData Central SR Legacy 173468, Salt, table, https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/173468/nutrients, accessed 2026-10-26, listing 1 tsp = 6 g, 1 tbsp = 18 g and 1 cup = 292 g in US measures. Units convention: US tablespoon, teaspoon and cup throughout. An Australian 20 mL tablespoon is not mixed with these figures, and no metric measure is used on this card. Proxy status: rows I1 and I2 use the generic whole-sesame-seed ratio because the purchased brand and roast state were not provided, so both are labeled proxies rather than exact matches; row I3 uses the generic table-salt ratio because the salt type was not provided. Fine and kosher salts are not interchangeable - table salt at 18 g per US tbsp, Morton's kosher at 16 g and Diamond Crystal at 8 g, a spread of about 2.25 times for the same 10 g - so the salt volume is a cross-check only and the 10 g weight remains the production control.

notes.heading: Volume arithmetic and rounding
notes.text: I1: 100 g divided by 8.875 g per US tbsp = 11.27 tbsp, shown as approximately 11.3 tbsp, rounded to the nearest 0.1 tbsp. I2: 20 g divided by 8.875 g per US tbsp = 2.25 tbsp, shown as approximately 2.25 tbsp, rounded to the nearest 0.05 tbsp. I3: 10 g divided by 6 g per US tsp = 1.67 tsp, shown as approximately 1.7 tsp, rounded to the nearest 0.1 tsp. Cup equivalents at 142 g per US cup are approximately 0.70 cup for I1 and approximately 0.14 cup for I2. Every volume on this card is a derived approximation: where an exact measure is needed, weigh the ingredient and measure the spoon.
